prompt: Write a Supplier factory that hands out a brand-new empty list on every get() call, plus a generic orDefault helper that falls back when a supplier yields null. Complete both methods in Suppliers.
explanation: A Supplier<T> is the functional interface for deferred creation: nothing happens until get() is called. Returning () -> new ArrayList<>() means every get() runs the lambda body again, producing a fresh list -- returning an already-built list would hand out the same object every time. The generic orDefault shows the common call-then-null-check pattern that Optional.ofNullable(...).orElse(...) also expresses.
hints: The supplier lambda takes no arguments: () -> something.
Make sure the 'new ArrayList' happens INSIDE the lambda body, not before the return statement.
In orDefault, store s.get() in a local variable so you call the supplier exactly once, then null-check it.
